key_insight: Selective, low-cost guidance applied in latent space (via selective TFG and small Latent-Control Heads) yields fine-grained controllable audio diffusion while avoiding expensive decoder backprop, dramatically lowering inference compute per step.
problem_solved: Provides a way to get fine-grained, controllable audio generation without retraining or heavy inference-time compute caused by backpropagating through large decoders.
method: Identify and quantify the decoder backpropagation bottleneck in existing guidance-based audio diffusion methods.
Selective TFG — apply guidance only to selected latent / time–frequency components to concentrate compute where it matters and reduce per-step cost.
Latent-Control Heads (LatCHs) — attach lightweight control heads in latent space that enable steering (and producing guidance signals) without full decoder backprop.
impact: Enables practitioners to add powerful, fine-grained controls to latent audio diffusion models with much lower inference cost and memory, making controllable audio generation faster and more practical for low-resource or real-time scenarios.

paper_title: Low-Resource Guidance for Controllable Latent Audio Diffusion
